questions.question: Describe the four phases of the business cycle with their signature conditions, and state the practical definition of a recession.
questions.expected_answer: Upswing/expansion: production rising, hiring, incomes and spending feeding each other — injections outrunning leakages. Peak: the upper turning point — capacity strained, jobs plentiful, prices pressing upward, skills short. Downswing/contraction: production falling, retrenchments, shrinking incomes and spending — deep and prolonged, a recession, formally two consecutive quarters of declining real GDP. Trough: the lower turning point — weakest activity, but with recovery's seeds: low costs, eased interest rates, accumulated replacement demand. The cycle recurs but not on a timetable.

questions.question: Classify indicators by timing with reasons and examples, and explain the four movements inside a time series.
questions.expected_answer: Leading indicators (building plans, new orders, vehicle sales, share prices, confidence) bend first because they are today's decisions about tomorrow's activity — they warn. Coincident indicators (current production, retail sales, employment) confirm the present. Lagging indicators (unemployment, inventories, outstanding loans) turn after — firms retrench and rehire late — certifying the past. The Reserve Bank compiles composites and dates SA's cycle. Time series mix four movements: the long-term TREND; the multi-year CYCLICAL wave; the SEASONAL within-year calendar pattern (hence seasonally adjusted figures); and IRREGULAR one-off shocks — classify before declaring a turn.

questions.question: Distinguish exogenous from endogenous causes, and trace the effects of a downswing across society.
questions.expected_answer: Exogenous causes originate outside the system: drought, wars, pandemics, and — critical for South Africa — world commodity price swings. Endogenous causes arise inside: waves of optimism/pessimism feeding investment then snapping; credit expanding in good times and tightening in bad; injections and leakages over- and under-shooting equilibrium. Real cycles mix both — an outside shock on an inside amplifier. Downswing effects: unemployment rising, hardest on the least skilled; incomes and profits shrinking; government revenue falling as grant needs rise; poverty deepening; investment postponed, weakening the next upswing.
